liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Passenger** (5 reviews): Brent is cutting loose on Passenger; Reviewer calls this the coolest Passenger heard from any year, with explosive dynamics [5][7][8][10][11]
- **Peggy O** (1 review): Listener names Peggy-O as one of the show's highlights [4]
- **High Time** (1 review): Reviewer likes the High Time [11]
- **Ship Of Fools** (1 review): Reviewer likens Jerry's Ship of Fools delivery to Cold Rain, alternately begging and commanding the listener [13]
- **Terrapin Station** (1 review): Listener names Terrapin Station as one of the show's highlights [4]
- **Playin' In The Band** (1 review): Playin' runs about twenty minutes [5]
- **Black Peter** (1 review): Black Peter runs about seventeen minutes [5]

## The recordings

- **gd1979-11-10.152823.sbd.dalton.miller.clugston.flac16** (recommended): soundboard; 24 songs; 190 min; rated 5/5 by 1 [1]
- **gd79-11-10.sbd.clugston.14108.sbeok.shnf**: matrix (soundboard mixed with audience mics); 24 songs; 181 min; rated 3.42/5 by 12 [2]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the recording decent sounding [6]
- **gd1979-11-10.sbd.willy.10457.shnf**: soundboard; 22 songs; 158 min; rated 4/5 by 3 [3]. Said about its sound: Recording begins mid El Paso, and High Time cuts in during its intro; Splices occur at 12:50 of Terrapin, in the post-song jam, and at 9:33 of Black Peter [3]

## Around the show

- Listener camped overnight at Crisler to get floor seats and cooled out afterward [4]
- Attendee recalls Jerry having guitar trouble, stopping several times while roadies fussed around him [9]
- Attendee remembers Bob stepping up his playing to compensate [9]
- Night was cold and rainy, which suited the opening Cold Rain [10]
- Soundboard was made for a friend who got married at the show; Healy was best man [10]
- Reviewer says this was Brent's first time playing Cold Rain and Snow with the band, though not audible on this copy [13]
- Post-space section has almost forty minutes of music, unlike many shows from this era [6]
- Reviewer finds the show a bit mediocre for 1979, with better shows available [6]
- Reviewer hears some of the best 1979 playing, alongside the Nassau shows, with Jerry in fine form [12]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd1979-11-10.152823.sbd.dalton.miller.clugston.flac16**: taped by Tim Dalton; transferred by Scott Clugston and Charlie Miller; source: Master Soundboard Cassettes > 1st generation cassettes > Tim Dalton's Beta PCM [1]. Also: Unknown audience source supplies some crowd sound and the first 1:51 of Cold Rain & Snow; David Lemieux's Taper's Section broadcast supplies the rest of Cold Rain, plus Minglewood, Peggy O and early El Paso [1]
- **gd79-11-10.sbd.clugston.14108.sbeok.shnf**: source: Soundboard [2]. Also: Master soundboard cassette to reel to DAT to CDR, with audience patches, via Scott Clugston [2]
- **gd1979-11-10.sbd.willy.10457.shnf**: taped by Audio discs provided by Paul B; transferred by Willy; source: SBD>MR>DAT>CDR [3]. Also: Audio discs were provided by Paul B; retracked and edited with CD Wave, Shntool and CE2K [3]

## Art and photos

- Poster by Worthpoint: [AOR 4.200 Original Grateful Dead Poster Crisler Arena | #2062379170](https://www.worthpoint.com/worthopedia/aor-200-original-grateful-dead-poster-2062379170) [17]
- Poster by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Poster - Crisler Arena](https://www.dead.net/archives/1979/artwork/poster-crisler-arena) [18]
- Fan art by Pandora: [Alabama Getaway (Live at Crisler Arena, Ann Arbor, November 10, 1979)](https://www.pandora.com/artist/grateful-dead/road-trips-vol-1-no-1-new-haven-coliseum-new-haven-ct-10-25-79-the-spectrum-philadelphia-pa-11-6-79-memorial-auditorium-buffalo-ny-11-8-70-crisler-arena-ann-arbor-mi-11-9-79-11-10-79-live/alabama-getaway-live-at-crisler-arena-ann-arbor-november-10-1979/TR63pqcmn34J3ZZ) [19]
- Poster by Worthpoint: [AOR 4.200 Original Grateful Dead Poster Crisler Arena | #2062379170](https://www.worthpoint.com/worthopedia/aor-200-original-grateful-dead-poster-2062379170) [20]
